name: High-volume message sender
problem: Queue-based sender with rate limits, dedupe, retries and delivery-status reconciliation.
limits: Real Redis Streams and Lua operations; destinations and message contents are synthetic and no messages are sent externally. A worker physically exits after receipt creation but before sender ACK/status; replacement processing reconciles the existing receipt. Retryable timeouts are injected before delivery; Redis enforces the shared rate schedule. Exactly-once sink effects rely on sink-side idempotency in Redis, not on an arbitrary email/SMS provider. Redis server crashes, durable failover and multiple hosts are not covered; this benchmark disables persistence for an isolated temporary server. evidence/reconciliation.json retains per-message receipts, counts and queue status.
next: Add provider adapters with idempotency contracts, durable Redis configuration and multi-worker load tests.
